chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Isma'il ibn Sahl from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami from al-Kahili from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): that he was asked

about a man whose mother married him while he was absent. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The marriage is valid; if the groom wishes, he may accept it, and if he wishes, he may reject it. And if the groom rejects the marriage arranged for him, the dowry remains obligatory upon his mother.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mother marries her absent adult son without his prior consent?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of 'kafala' (guardianship) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the validity of the contract and the option of ratification for the absent adult. It highlights the principle of financial accountability, stipulating that if the son exercises his right to reject the marriage, the mother bears the cost of the dowry as she acted as the contracting party. This ruling underscores the balance between parental authority and the individual's autonomy in marital contracts within the Shia legal tradition.
